Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Maria, DOB: 22/03/1990, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: Not recorded
- Referring GP: Doctor Kumar, Practice: Not recorded, Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Illness-related anxiety / health anxiety (patient self-described as "a little bit hypochondriac"; acute excessive worry about serious neurological disease in context of new headache)
- Secondary: Migraine with visual aura (provisional medical diagnosis by GP; supported as "High" likelihood in DDx)
- Tertiary: Vestibular/basilar migraine variant (DDx: Medium likelihood — dizziness prominent) / other acute neurological causes to exclude (e.g., SAH, intracranial mass) — listed for consideration per DDx

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Took paracetamol (time: ~3 hours after headache onset). Clinician recommended ibuprofen and an antiemetic (dose/route/frequency not documented); clinician also suggested sugary/carbonated drink (e.g., Coke). 
- Allergies/ADRs: No known drug allergies reported.
- Past Medical History: Kidney stones. No other chronic illnesses recorded.

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Patient reports being "a little bit hypochondriac" (self-report). No formal psychiatric diagnoses recorded.
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): Not recorded.
- Family History: Mother has migraines and hypothyroidism.

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Not recorded.
- Social Support: Not recorded.
- Occupation/Education: Not recorded.
- Alcohol Use: Not recorded.
- Smoking/Substance Use: Not recorded.
- Key Stressors: Acute onset of severe, unfamiliar headache with visual disturbance leading to significant worry about serious neurological disease (brain tumour, stroke).

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Cooperative, engaged with clinician, visibly worried/anxious.
- Mood & Affect: Anxious, concerned about physical health; affect congruent with mood.
- Speech & Thought: Speech coherent, relevant; thoughts focused on explaining symptoms and expressing concern about serious illness.
- Perception: Reports visual disturbances described as "blurred vision" and "zigzag lines" (visual aura/visual phenomena).

Cognition:
- Orientation: Oriented to person and context in consultation.
- Attention/Concentration: Able to attend and answer clinician's questions though distracted by symptoms.
- Memory: Not recorded.
- Insight & Judgement: Demonstrates insight into tendency for health anxiety (self-described) and appropriate help-seeking behaviour; judgement appropriate in seeking GP assessment.

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Not recorded.
- Appetite: Not recorded.
- Motivation/Energy: Not recorded.
- Anxiety Symptoms: Excessive worry about having a brain tumour or stroke, hypervigilance to bodily symptoms, expressed nausea and vomiting (somatic symptom related to headache).

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: No suicidal ideation, self-harm intent or risk to others disclosed or observed. (Not recorded otherwise.)
- Protective Factors: Patient insight into health anxiety, engaged with GP, willing to follow recommended plan and attend assessment.
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low (no suicidal or self-harm ideation reported; patient seeking care).
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded.

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Family history of migraine; patient reports baseline tendency toward health anxiety ("a little bit hypochondriac").
- Precipitating factors: Sudden onset left-sided headache with visual phenomena, dizziness, nausea and vomiting — first episode of this pattern precipitating acute catastrophic illness fears.
- Perpetuating factors: Catastrophic interpretations (brain tumour/stroke), lack of prior experience with similar headaches, persistent symptoms (visual disturbance, nausea) increasing anxiety and hypervigilance.
- Protective factors: Insight, prompt presentation to GP, GP provision of likely diagnosis (migraine), immediate management plan and arranged follow-up.
- Integrative statement: Patient with pre-existing health anxiety experienced a first-time acute left-sided headache with visual aura and vomiting. Symptom pattern and family history support migraine as most likely cause (DDx high likelihood). Catastrophic illness beliefs are maintaining significant distress; prompt symptomatic treatment and early neurological reassessment are planned to reduce uncertainty and anxiety.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Illness-related anxiety / health anxiety
- Patient Goal(s): Understand cause of symptoms; reduce anxiety about having a brain tumour or stroke; feel reassured and able to cope with current symptoms.
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide timely assessment and information to reduce catastrophic misinterpretation; manage acute symptoms; arrange appropriate follow-up to exclude serious neurological pathology if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take recommended symptomatic medications as advised by GP (ibuprofen and an antiemetic; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Attend urgent neurological assessment / GP follow-up if symptoms do not improve.
  - Contact GP/practice if symptoms worsen or new neurological signs appear.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide and explain provisional diagnosis (probable migraine with aura) and expected time course (migraine may improve from 30–40 minutes after treatment but can last 4–72 hours).
  - Recommend symptomatic treatment: ibuprofen + antiemetic (dose/route/frequency not documented) and oral sugary/carbonated drink as an adjunct.
  - Arrange urgent neurological assessment / full neurological examination if no improvement or if new/worsening neurological signs.
  - Offer opportunity to cancel follow-up appointment if symptoms resolve prior to scheduled assessment.
  - Provide reassurance and education regarding likelihood of migraine and reasons for further assessment if indicated.

Secondary Problem: Acute migraine with visual aura (medical)
- Patient Goal(s): Relief of headache and associated symptoms (visual disturbance, nausea/vomiting, dizziness).
- Clinical Goal(s): Achieve symptom control and exclude serious intracranial pathology if symptoms persist/worsen.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take paracetamol already taken (no effect); take recommended ibuprofen and antiemetic as advised (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Limit movement that exacerbates symptoms; reduce exposure to screens if tolerated poorly (patient reported intolerance to screens).
  - Attend assessment for neurological examination if symptoms persist/worsen.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide/advise symptomatic medications (ibuprofen and antiemetic) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Advise on expected response timeframe; escalate care/arrange urgent neurological review or imaging if symptoms do not improve or if focal neurological signs emerge.
  - Document and follow-up outcome of neurological assessment.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Explanation that presentation is most consistent with migraine with aura (unilateral headache, visual 'zigzag' phenomena, photophobia, nausea/vomiting), expected duration (can be 4–72 hours), initial symptomatic treatments (ibuprofen + antiemetic, sugary/carbonated drink), and need for urgent neurological review if not improving.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - New or worsening focal neurological signs (e.g., limb weakness, slurred speech, new coordination problems).
  - Sudden onset "worst-ever" headache or thunderclap headache.
  - Loss of consciousness, progressive reduced consciousness, persistent vomiting or neck stiffness.
  - Any deterioration in level of alertness or breathing difficulties.
  (These signs were discussed as reasons to seek urgent review / are included in DDx considerations.)
- Coping Strategies:
  - Follow recommended symptomatic treatment plan.
  - Rest and minimize movement that exacerbates symptoms.
  - Limit screen exposure if photophobia/intolerance reported.
  - Maintain contact with GP/practice and attend arranged assessment.

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes — patient agreed verbally to plan and follow-up.
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded.
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded.
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable / Not recorded.
- Review Date: Urgent neurological assessment planned for same day if symptoms persist; exact date/time not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Illness-related anxiety / Health anxiety (High) — Justification: Patient explicitly reports being "a little bit hypochondriac" and expresses marked worry that current symptoms represent a brain tumour or stroke; anxiety is the dominant psychological presentation.
- Acute stress reaction / Adjustment to acute medical symptoms (Medium) — Justification: First-time, sudden severe headache with distressing symptoms has precipitated significant acute worry and concern; situational stress response plausible given sudden onset and uncertainty.

Quality checks
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs and focused neurological examination not documented; no imaging or laboratory results recorded; precise medication prescriptions (drug doses/route/frequency) not documented; no formal psychiatric history beyond patient self-report; no emergency contact details.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None major — transcript and DDx both support migraine with aura as most likely. DDx lists other neurological causes (SAH, mass) for exclusion; clinician appropriately planned urgent review if not improving. (Conflict noted: none.)
- Transcript quality notes: Brief loss of audio/connection occurred during consultation ("we are losing connection"); some pauses and overlapping speech; overall key history and plan documented.
